card.name: Small words in old formal prose
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as in, with, any, the, a and and inside long, formal sentences in 18th and 19th century historical or scientific writing. They often come right before an abstract noun such as regard, approbation, hope or light.

modes.label: Preposition before abstract noun
modes.description: The word in or with begins a phrase of attitude or regard, as in held in regard or seen with approbation.
modes.example: on which account it was held<< in>> great regard by the Egyptians.

modes.label: Other linking words in archaic sentences
modes.description: An article, conjunction or verb sits partway through a formal clause in old narrative or official writing.
modes.example: an honor<< and>> responsibility I thought very great.

card.plain: It fires on little connecting words in old-fashioned, formal writing, where an abstract noun usually comes next.
